description:
Functional specifications covered with associated files to edit/add: lib/zaq/agent/opaque_aliases.ex and narrowly required Factory context/callback code; test/zaq/agent/opaque_aliases_test.exs and new Action alias tests. Add private-consumer output expansion by reusing action_schema/alias_paths/maybe_map_scoped traversal rather than manually traversing Record fields. Use the exact logical-server opaque_alias_scope already used by Factory input/output interception and history hydration. Canonical signed values remain private runtime contracts; the model sees aliases only on schema-declared paths. Do not make aliases authorization grants or globally resolve them by token text.
Tests to add before implementation: real Factory before_tool_call/after_tool_call -> Record list input aliases -> validated Action -> aliased output -> private expansion -> output validation. Verify same-scope round-trip; missing/wrong/expired scope, unknown alias and tampered signed record reject without mutation. Unrelated strings matching alias prefixes stay unchanged; nested lists/permissions traverse only declared paths; direct canonical output works. Preserve history alias lifetime across requests in one logical server and ensure separate servers cannot redeem each other's aliases.
Branches/paths validated: canonical/aliased Records, nested schema paths, ToolResult wrappers and effects preservation, input versus output traversal, schema failure, actor-independent alias lookup followed by separate authorization. Never clear logical-server history aliases merely to clear per-request selections.
Mocking plan: real isolated RuntimeStore/Factory schema mapping; unique runtime scope per test and cleanup. No global alias store stubs or internal authorization mocks.
Documentations to update for both code and docs/ related content: OpaqueAliases public expansion contract and docs/services/agent.md alias lifetime/private consumer boundary.
Action reuse assessment: extend OpaqueAliases; existing expand_tool_call and alias_tool_result already own schema traversal but do not expand tool output for the reducer. Local-only adapter with no new Action or tool. Input Action schema/output/trusted scope -> canonical output or scoped error; no provider I/O, delivery or permission bypass. Consumers: StreamEvents next, existing Factory/history preserved; PR7 consumers deferred. Validate separate server isolation and public redaction.

Implementation constraints: This is a proposed plan only. The current request authorizes setup and Beadwork planning, not implementation, commits, pushes, rebases or publication. Read AGENTS.md, docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md, docs/exec-plans/PLAN_STRATEGY.md, docs/action-reuse.md, docs/testing-approach.md, docs/documentation.md, docs/conventions.md and docs/code-quality.md before later execution; read the owning service guide and each touched module's @moduledoc. Agent work also follows docs/services/agent.md#harness-critical-checks-for-coding-agents. Recheck live source/contracts after PR5 advances. Preserve existing test behavior; if an assertion/scenario must change, record old/proposed behavior and obtain specific human approval first. No such changes are approved here. New unit/integration/property tests are immediate and written before production code. Keep real internal boundaries and isolated fixture/process state; inject runtime dependencies through established opts/context and Zaq.Config.get/4 where relevant, without global configuration mutation. Follow the authoritative validation lifecycle in docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md; do not treat historical/reference runs as current validation. PR5 owns delivery execution/outcomes; PR7 owns RunAgent, NotifyPerson and notification/workflow integration.
title: [zaq-pi3.4] Expand selection output aliases through the existing schema traversal
